body:
Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (0) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Unrecorded starts can spawn another lead ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: 084270e

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>Docs and design spec now require retrying the LEAD-STARTED post up to 3 times, and state that a
>LEAD-STARTED (including an unconfirmed one) holds off any further start for 30 minutes, with the
>watchdog and architect told to wait for LEAD ONLINE rather than start another lead.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>start_lead() reports a successful fire even when post_quietly() fails to record LEAD-STARTED,
>leaving the watchdog without its record of the new session. If the next watchdog run occurs before
>that session posts LEAD ONLINE, it can fire another takeover for the same stall; the architect's
>new instructions also treat an absent marker as a reason to start one by hand.
>
>
2. A retry can start two leads ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: 3b98290

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>Unknown-outcome failures (timeouts, lost replies, HTTP 200 without routine_fire) are classified as
>possibly-started: start-lead posts "LEAD-STARTED: unconfirmed (...)" and exits 0 so callers don't
>retry; definite failures still exit 1 for retry. Docs and the exit-code table were updated to
>match.</what_was_the_impact>
><parameter name="relevant_diff_lines_start">2832
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>start_lead() returns exit 1 when fire() times out or receives a response it cannot recognize,
>even though the task may already have started a session. The handover instructions tell the lead to
>retry immediately, while no lease or LEAD-STARTED marker necessarily exists to stop the second
>fire.
>
>

3. Buzz instructions can start a second lead ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: 084270e

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The LEAD-SILENT takeover section now states that one takeover lead is started in exactly one of two
>ways, never both: the architect starts it (Matthew does not start a lead himself), or the architect
>gives Matthew the takeover line to start. This removes the unconditional second start that could
>launch a duplicate takeover.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>The revised LEAD-SILENT instructions say the architect may start the takeover itself or give
>Matthew a takeover line, but the next step tells Matthew to start a lead unconditionally. If the
>architect already fired the task, following both steps can launch another takeover instead of
>stopping after the first start.
>
>
4. Watchdog can take over from a working lead ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: d4cec85

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>The diff makes the watchdog hold off takeover starts while any trusted lead message (including a
>STATUS) is within silent-after. The stall episode's "sign" now includes trusted lead messages of any
>kind, and alarm_stage/start hold-off uses it. LEAD.md adds a rule to post STATUS before long steps.
>Also an alarm is still posted, but a live lead that posts is not taken over.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>cmd_watchdog passes takeover=lease_of(values)[0] != "none" to alarm_stage, which calls
>watchdog_start as soon as silent_after has passed since the last LEAD-STARTED or LEAD ONLINE.
>Nothing checks whether the lease holder is still alive. Progress counts only step and pr changes,
>mission-branch pushes and merges, so a live lead whose builders run past three hours with no merge
>is enough to trigger it. The takeover lead runs lease take --takeover and the working lead loses
>the lease mid-build. Before this PR the watchdog only alarmed, and the architect checked whether the
>lead was alive before giving out a takeover line.
>
>
5. A failed post-decision lead leaves the room silent forever ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: 69463dc

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>N/A
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>pending_decision skips a DECISION-n as soon as any trusted LEAD-STARTED is newer than it.
>After that, cmd_watchdog prints quiet: step is waiting for owner… on every later run, because
>the step is still waiting for owner and the lease is still released. So if the lead started after
>the decision (by the watchdog or the architect) never joins, for example because its session ended
>at once, ran out of usage, or the fire returned 200 but the run died, the watchdog never alarms and
>never starts another lead, and the room stalls with no buzz until someone reads it by hand.
>
>
View medium (1)
6. Other processes can read the fire token ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: 084270e

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>N/A
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>fire() embeds the bearer token in the curl argument vector rather than passing it through a
>protected input channel. On a host where another local process can inspect process arguments during
>the request, that process can copy the credential used to fire the project's lead task.
>
>

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
